scope: After inducing glutathionylation of SMYD2 in vitro, SMYD2 was subjected to click reaction with biotin-DDE-alkyne
The digest solution was added to streptavidin-agarose beads (Invitrogen) (50°L) in PBS and incubated for 2°h.

Bound peptides were then eluted by 2% hydrazine in PBS (3°x 30°L, pH 7.4). Eluted fractions were combined and acidified with 5% formic acid. The sample was desalted by C18 silica zip-tip (Millipore) and analyzed by Bruker MALDI-TOF/TOF ultrafleXtreme instrument

For ESI MS/MS analysis, eluted peptides were separated by UHPLC reverse phase chromatography with an EASY-nLC 1000 liquid chromatography system (Thermo) and introduced into an Orbitrap FUSION mass spectrometer (Thermo).

This project utilizes an approach consisting of azido-glutathione, a single purified protein, and an oxidant to form disulfide bonds between the azide modified glutathione and the cysteine residues of the protein.

The protein of interest, e.g. SMYD2, (50-100 ug), is reacted with azido-glutathione, in the presence of diamide to provide glutathionylated SMYD2. This is reacted with biotin-DDE-alkyne which is a biotin probe that can be cleaved with hydrazine. The protein is digested with trypsin overnight at 37 C, and the peptides were allowed to bind to streptavidin-agarose beads and then eluted with 2% hydrazine in PBS.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry analysis was performed on in vitro glutathionylated purified SMYD2 protein, which was then affinity-captured using biotin-alkyne and streptavidin beads prior to digestion and LC-MS/MS.
